unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 10 (AFTER PREP)-LEVEL: B2.2 - THEME 4: FAMILY LIFE & HOME

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will write and act-out role plays about family conflicts in pairs. They will discuss, brainstorm and list the conflicts that could be in families. They will write a role play and/ or dialogue for the problem they choose from the list. Then, they will act out the role play they have chosen in the class in pairs. They may record their role plays as well. They may use accessories, clothing, visuals or videos while performing the role play. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''family life and home with its components such as designing and decorating family homes; housing problems and family conflicts; family traditions and customs about food'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in after prep year 10 of an upper secondary school may know what designing and decorating family homes; housing problems and family conflicts; family traditions and customs about food mean in their as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in a foreign language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in after prep year 10 of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''family life and home'' and also some necessary structures in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in after prep year 10 of upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''family life and home with its components such as designing and decorating family homes; housing problems and family conflicts; family traditions and customs about food'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about housing problems and family conflicts in English by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: Home Renovation Debate The teacher shows some visuals for designing and decorating family homes, housing problems, and family conflicts (e.g. installing a device, a broken window, or a family discussion). The class discusses each visual through identification of what it represents and the possible conflicts it might cause. For example, a broken window might lead to blame or disagreement about repairs. Then, students work in groups of three to four. In groups, students choose a conflict from the visuals and act it out. Each student takes a role such as ''a parent, a sibling, or a mediator'' and uses target words such as ''to urge'', ''to criticise'', or ''to insist''. For example, in a conflict about renovating the kitchen or living room, the father could say ''We should start with the kitchen because it’s more useful''. The mother could say, ''But the living room looks bad and everyone sees it first''. The mediator could say, ''Let’s fix the kitchen first and then do the living room later''. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on accurate use of the language with target vocabulary, grammar, and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To talk about housing problems and family conflicts in English by using the target vocabulary. Activity 1: Home Renovation Debate The teacher shows some simple visuals of home-related problems (e.g. a broken window, a messy room, or someone installing a TV) and asks guiding questions like ''What is this?'' or ''Is there a problem?'' to help students describe what they see to use target vocabulary and target grammar. (e.g. ''The window is broken''). Target vocabulary such as ''fix, angry, clean, should'' is introduced with repetition and gestures. Students are divided into small groups and choose one picture to role-play. Each student is given a simple role (Parent 1, Parent 2, Child, or Mediator) and sentence starters like ''Let’s fix the...'', ''I think we should...'', or ''No, the TV is okay''. They perform short dialogues based on the given situation by using the target words and grammar. The teacher gives supportive feedback for the use of language including the target vocabulary, grammar, and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
